content_fields.title: Test that the application is not vulnerable to JSON Hijacking
content_fields.description: Wrap collection responses in a JSON object so the reply is never a bare top-level array that a foreign page can read.
content_fields.finding: The endpoint returns a top-level JSON array of order records to a GET request, which is the classic shape exploited by JSON hijacking when the response is reachable with ambient credentials.
content_fields.current_code:
@router.get("/orders", response_model=List[schemas.Order])
def get_orders(
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    skip: int = 0,
    limit: int = 100,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
    auth=Depends(RolesBasedAuthChecker([UserRole.CUSTOMER])),
):
    orders = (
        db.query(Order)
        .filter(Order.user_id == current_user.id)
        .offset(skip)
        .limit(limit)
        .all()
    )
    return orders
criteria: No endpoint returns a top-level JSON array.
Collection endpoints respond with an object whose payload sits under a named key.
Responses are served with `Content-Type: application/json` and are not executable as script.
